headline: Data Engineer at Google | Helping people land data jobs | Ex - Optum, Paytm | PEC’21
text:
If I have an Data Engineering interview in the a month, my strategy would be:

1️⃣ Deep-dive into core SQL fundamental concepts.
2️⃣ Daily solve 10 high-frequency SQL problems asked in interviews.
3️⃣ Solve 20–30 Python coding challenges on data structures and algorithmic logic.
4️⃣ Solidify PySpark essentials, building a strong foundation in the Spark ecosystem.
5️⃣ Learn about differences among RDDs, DataFrames, and Datasets.
6️⃣ Practice 10 PySpark questions daily.
7️⃣ Revise Data Warehousing methodologies, focusing on modern architectural patterns.
8️⃣ Learn Data Modeling.
9️⃣ Go through common interview questions.
🔟 Read blogs on interview experiences for the company you're applying to.

text:
SQL vs Pandas vs PySpark — One Cheatsheet to Rule Them All 🔥

If you work with data, you’ve probably jumped between
 👉 SQL
 👉 Pandas
 👉 PySpark
Same logic.
 Different syntax.
 Different scale.

So I created a side-by-side cheatsheet comparing core operations across all three — from filtering and joins to aggregations and null handling.


📌 Why this matters:
SQL → Best for databases & BI
Pandas → Fast analysis on local data
PySpark → Distributed processing at scale
Knowing when and how to use each is what separates a data analyst from a data engineer.
